title: effort ledger: solo 2-week sprint notes
body:
Purpose: lightweight personal ledger for a 2-week solo sprint. Not a formal PRD—brain-dump, timeboxes, micro-OKRs, and quick retro so I don’t lose signals.

Sprint horizon: 2025-01-06 -> 2025-01-19 (two focused weeks)
Context: post-holiday sprint, refocusing on core throughput wins + a small customer triage flow. Goal is to prove 1 low-risk perf tweak and unblock a dependent customer demo.

Micro-Objective (one-liner): deliver two small, measurable wins that reduce customer friction and give a defensible perf headline for the demo.

Draft Key Results (micro):
- KR1: Reduce 95p inference latency for local checkout test from ~160ms -> <=130ms on p3-small by Jan 16 (measurement: 1k-run prefix distribution)
- KR2: Merge and ship PR that adds prefix cache toggle + docs for customers (target: merged and smoke-tested by Jan 12)
- KR3: Clear the top 3 customer questions in the triage thread and hand over final notes to AE (target: Jan 15)

Signals I’ll watch (why these):
- Build time: how long experiments take (goal <2h per iteration)
- 95p latency delta in controlled harness (easy to regress; primary signal)
- Number of outstanding customer questions (<=0 by handoff)
- Personal energy: days with >4 focused hours (track as truth)

Energy budget / timeboxes (two-week plan):
- Week A (Jan 6–10): 60% engineering experiments + perf harness; 20% PR/docs; 20% customer triage
- Week B (Jan 13–17): 40% followups, 40% rollout + smoke, 20% retro/writeup + knowledge share
- Daily timebox: 9:30–13:00 focus block = deep work; afternoons for async/collab
- Saturday quick check (30m) only if critical — avoid work creep

Experiment log (shorthand):
- 01/07: baseline run (1k samples): median 78ms, 95p 162ms. Notes: KV cache looks warm-ish; batching small.
- 01/08: try continuous batching tweak in runtime: reduced overhead for small seqs; 95p -> 148ms. Rough win.
- 01/09: tuned kernel selection hint for shorter seqs (force fp16 path): 95p -> 136ms but slight jitter on p3-small after 300 samples. Need more runs.
- 01/10: rollback kernel hint, instead add tiny synthetic KV warm path; 95p -> 128ms stable across 2k samples. Candidate change.

PR & docs timeline:
- PR draft created (github.com/redwood-inference/pull/312). Contains runtime flag + unit tests + a short README snippet.
- Needs: one more perf test, a changelog entry, and a short example in hosted-api quickstart.
- Blocking: need SRE approval for metric exposure (ticket opened JIRA-554)

Customer triage notes:
- Thread: slack://thread/C02ABCDEF/1612345678
- Top asks: reproducibility steps for higher-latency observations; can we provide a canned harness? Answer: yes, created short instructions and a small harness script. Sent to AE on Jan 14.
- Concern: customer worried about cost when increasing batch size. Reply: showed cost vs latency plot (sharing in handoff doc).

Quantitative snapshots (end of week A):
- Focus hours recorded: 4/5 working days hit >4h deep blocks
- Experiment iterations: 6 full runs
- Candidate PRs: 1 (active), followups: 2 small tasks
- Customer questions remaining: 1 (answer in progress)

Immediate blockers / unknowns:
- SRE signoff may take longer than expected if we add new metrics. Contingency: ship behind a feature flag.
- Small jitter on p3 after long runs; might be noise. Need a 10k-sample run to be confident (time cost).

Quick retrospective notes (end of sprint):
- What went well: quick wins found by iterating small runtime hints; docs + PR streamlined once I timeboxed writing blocks.
- What surprised me: the perf delta from the synthetic KV warm path was larger than expected; saved ~20–30ms at 95p.
- What to change: schedule an explicit 2-hour weekly review with SRE early in next sprint to avoid last-minute approval delays.

Next sprint ideas (seeded):
- Follow up: automation to run 5k-sample smoke in CI nightly for critical workloads (proof-of-concept)
- Triage: convert the harness + results into a short notebook for AE to reproduce locally
- Personal: try swimlane focus (two mornings per week dedicated solely to perf experiments)

Todo (concrete):
- [ ] finish extended 10k-sample run and attach results to PR (target Jan 16)
- [ ] add changelog + quickstart snippet to PR (target Jan 12) — in progress
- [ ] follow up SRE for metric exposure path; propose feature-flag guard (target Jan 13)
- [ ] finalize handoff note for AE + attach harness (target Jan 15)

Loose thoughts / heuristics (personal):
- Aim for visible, measurable wins; it’s often better to ship a small, well-instrumented change than an ambitious one with uncertain rollout.
- Keep a two-line summary at top of PR for non-engineers (helps AEs and product folks quickly evaluate impact).
- Timeboxes force writing; writing clarifies assumptions and reduces rework.

End log: capture commit ids and final numbers here after merge. For now: candidate change flagged for ship behind feature flag; early data promising.

Notes-to-self: archive results to personal perf-notes folder and link from AE handoff doc. Don’t forget to update my sprint tracker (notion).
